message.content:
I need to find RPC handler methods in this repository that can transitively cause an outbound HTTP request to a user-configured URL (like webhooks, notifications, etc.). I need:

1. At least three RPC handler method names
2. The single function where all those code paths converge before actually making the outbound HTTP request

Steps:
- First, understand the repo structure (what kind of project is this?)
- Look for RPC handler definitions (could be gRPC, JSON-RPC, or custom RPC)
- Look for outbound HTTP request functionality (webhooks, notifications, HTTP client calls to user-configured URLs)
- Trace from the HTTP-sending function back to find what RPC handlers can trigger it
- Also trace from RPC handlers forward to find which ones lead to outbound HTTP requests
- Identify the convergence/bottleneck function where all paths meet

Search broadly - look for things like:
- webhook, hook, callback, notify, notification, dispatch, deliver, send
- http.Post, http.Do, httpClient, fetch, request, axios, got
- RPC, handler, service, server, method
- Any configuration of URLs that get called

Report: the handler method names, the convergence function name, and the file paths for each.

Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## The Single Convergence Function

**`Post`** in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`, line 120.

All code paths converge here. The call chain is:

```
RPC Handler
  -> DispatchMemo*Webhook()           (memo_service_webhooks.go)
    -> dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook()   (memo_service_webhooks.go, line 48)
      -> webhook.PostAsync()          (webhook.go, line 184)
        -> webhook.Post()             (webhook.go, line 120)  <-- CONVERGENCE POINT
          -> safeClient.Do(req)       (the actual outbound HTTP POST)
```

`PostAsync` enqueues the payload into a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`); 4 goroutines started in `init()` dequeue from that channel and call `Post()`. The `Post` function constructs an `http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, ...)`, optionally signs it with HMAC-SHA256, and executes it via `safeClient.Do(req)`. The `safeClient` includes SSRF protection that blocks connections to reserved/private IP ranges.

`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (line 30 of `memo_service_webhooks.go`) also calls `webhook.PostAsync()` directly (without going through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`), but it still converges at the same `Post` function.
